source.title: On the Role of Attention Heads in Large Language Model Safety
source.authors: Zhenhong Zhou; Haiyang Yu; Xinghua Zhang; Rongwu Xu; Fei Huang; Kun Wang; Yang Liu; Jun-Feng Fang; Yong-Bin Li

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-query compliance after attention-head ablations, a different intervention from the fine-tuning and token-position tests in the claim. Its head-ablation results directly test whether safety can be localized to a small parameter set; an affirmative opening is also tested as a jailbreak condition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports head-ablation ASR outcomes, including outcomes under an affirmative opening. It does not test fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples, per-token KL across response positions, suffix attacks, decoding changes, or methods for deepening safety. Values used only to select heads or rank them are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study ablates individually attributed attention heads (about 0.006% of parameters for one head) in Llama-2-7b-chat and Vicuna-7b-v1.5 and measures harmful-query ASR. This directly tests V5, that safety sits in a small set of weights, with a method other than the originals' fine-tuning. Appendix E's affirmative 'Sure, here is' prefill also gives a V4 result, though with no matched no-prefill baseline. Neither original source is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a few sparse attention heads are crucial for refusing harmful queries, and that ablating them, mainly by flattening attention weights rather than scaling head output, sharply raises ASR with little helpfulness cost. They argue the heads act as safety feature extractors. Safety heads overlap across models fine-tuned from the same base, which they read as evidence that pre-training shapes safety. They add that the heads also support course-correction after an affirmative opening.
record.recipe_differences: The paper attributes safety heads by measuring outcomes after attention-head ablation; it does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign examples as in the cited fine-tuning claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured effect varies with ablation method (Undifferentiated Attention versus Scaling Contribution), attribution level (dataset-level versus specific-query), dataset, and whether an affirmative opening or system prompt is used. The authors also report that larger head groups can reduce ASR after a threshold, partly because nonsensical outputs count as failures.

fits_no_version.finding: Loading base-model (pre-alignment) attention parameters into aligned Llama-2-7b-chat keeps safety close to the aligned model (Fig. 6a). Safety heads also overlap heavily between Llama-2-7b-chat and Vicuna, both fine-tuned from Llama-2-7b (Fig. 5b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The attention-head component of refusal comes largely from pre-training rather than alignment tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Base Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B with a URIAL in-context system prompt refuse almost all harmful queries (ASR at most about 0.05) (Fig. 15a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context system prompts alone produce refusal in unaligned base models.

record.problems: ASR is rule-based: generations containing listed rejection keywords are judged harmless; short generations and repeated outputs are also treated as harmless. The authors note that output style changes after parameter modification and manually expanded the keyword list. Some plotted results have no exact values in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not reported for most outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: At most 60 rows were retained. Omitted further figure-level ASR details include disaggregated Figure 2 bars, individual-head heatmaps and additional ablation curves in Figures 4, 11, 12 and 17; these are not fully numerically stated in the text. Helpfulness results in Figure 6 were omitted because they measure zero-shot task scores rather than the claim versions' harmful-compliance outcomes. Table 5's separate Vicuna ablation increments were also omitted after prioritizing the affirmative-opening test and the Llama-2-7b-chat numerical ablation results.

untested.parts: Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, longer or graded prefills, and models other than Llama-2-7b-chat. There is no matched no-prefill control.
Non-attention parameter types (MLP, ranks, neurons) under the same method, and model families beyond Llama-2-7b derivatives.
Whether data or the training objective produces shallowness.

missing.what: ASR of the 'concatenated' model (base-model attention with aligned remaining weights) on three datasets; only a figure, not declared in rows_left_out.
ASR of base models under URIAL in-context alignment.

record.verdict_notes: ASR uses a broad rule-based keyword judge: 'However', 'harmful' and 'responsible' count as refusal, and short or repetitive outputs count as harmless. This likely understates compliance, especially in the Appendix E prefill test. Most inputs are direct or a simple non-native template with no system prompt; vanilla ASR is about 0.04 for Llama-2 and 0.27 for Vicuna. V4 evidence is thin: one short prefill, one model, no matched control. Mixed states within r51–r58 and r60 are left mostly as the reader set them.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence across aligned and base models' response positions.

The study tests an affirmative initial phrase and attention-head ablation, not adversarial suffixes or decoding changes; it does not isolate the effect of prefilling against a matched no-prefix condition.
The study tests attention heads, not low-rank safety parameters or whether the effect generalizes to other parameter types.
Whether safety-training data or objectives produce shallow safety.
Training to spread safety across response positions and robustness of such training.

reader_labels.reason: Ablating selected attention heads raises harmful-query ASR, including 0.04 to 0.64 for Llama-2-7b-chat and a three-head result with ∼0.018% parameter modification (r16,r18-r28,r39-r48).
